A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SKADA-Bench. All 34 pages of v1 and 45 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables and figures. Internal reporting inconsistencies are identifiable document issues rather than extraction gaps.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmarking experiments for shallow domain adaptation methods, including accuracies, validation-scorer analyses and computational timings in Table 2 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains original shallow-method experiments and reports additional deep-method evaluations, F1 results and scorer-ranking analyses in Tables 3, 21–22 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes a new DA algorithm, and the retained shallow methods have unchanged procedural descriptions. V2 adds published deep methods and MixVal as evaluated comparators; their architectures and validation settings extend the experiments rather than establish a new proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same four simulated shifts and eight real-world classification datasets across vision, NLP, tabular data and biosignals. The deep experiments reuse MNIST/USPS, Office31, OfficeHome and BCI. Their different input representations and architectures concern evaluation settings rather than new tasks or populations.

E2.justification: V2 Table 3 evaluates seven deep comparators: DeepCORAL, DAN, DANN, DeepJDOT, MCC, MDD and SPA, alongside source/target controls and LinOT. MixVal joins the evaluated scorers. Some appendix comparison sets also shrink: Table 13 omits TCA, TSL, JDOT and DASVM, all present in v1's Mushroom Table D.6.

E3.justification: The added deep experiments introduce raw-image/EEG inputs, dataset-specific CNN, ResNet50 and ShallowFBCSPNet architectures, and neural-network training schedules. They use one outer split and exclude CircV for computational reasons. Appendix E.4 also adds F1 evaluation. The original shallow nested-validation protocol and documented hyperparameter grids remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a check of whether conclusions persist under F1 and a statistical comparison of scorer rankings in Sections E.4–E.5. Existing scorer analyses extend to MixVal, and supervised-versus-unsupervised validation comparisons extend to deep methods. The original base-estimator sensitivity tables and runtime analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 4 adds pairwise Wilcoxon-based significance reporting for scorer rankings. V2 explicitly reports one outer split and no significance tests for the new deep experiments. The shallow experiments retain their five-split design, standard-deviation reporting and method-versus-source Wilcoxon testing practice.

E6.justification: Numerous shallow accuracies, rankings and selected scorers change, alongside new deep and F1 results. For example, Table 2 reports DASVM on 20NewsGroups as 0.68 with CircV in v1 and 0.87 with MixVal in v2; this is not a same-setting gain. V2 also corrects the main-table CORAL conditional-shift value from 0.66 to 0.76, matching the retained SVC appendix result.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 strengthens the subspace-shift definition: v2 requires equal projected feature marginals as well as equal label conditionals and states that the shift occurs in the orthogonal complement. V1 states only the conditional-invariance requirement. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: V1 positions the contribution around shallow DA benchmarking and realistic model selection. V2 adds an explicit shallow-versus-deep comparison contribution and concludes that deep methods' advantages depend on modality, architecture and tuning. Diverse dataset coverage and the central importance of realistic validation remain existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands applicability explanations: support overlap and near-uniform weights for reweighting, class count and target shift for mapping failures, and simple transformations as practical defaults. It adds semantic/style-disentanglement explanations for vision and limited-data/tuning limitations for deep BCI adaptation. V1's Amazon-review pretraining explanation is removed.

D1.justification: Tables 24–25 add dataset-specific neural architectures, batch sizes, optimizers, learning rates, epochs, schedulers and grids for seven deep methods; v2 also reports 244 GPU-hours and identifies MOABB access for BCI. Existing shallow grids and extension examples remain. Appendix release wording changes from already open-sourced to future availability, although the abstract retains the repository pointer.

R1.justification: V2 expands its positioning from a shallow-benchmarking gap to a claimed missing quantitative comparison of deep DA against shallow methods using pretrained features. Added literature supports reweighting limitations, target-shift failures, disentanglement, tabular/BCI comparisons and newer deep baselines. This goes beyond the accompanying citation-style changes and duplicate bibliographic entries.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the background, method and dataset prose remain. V2 locally rewrites the results discussion and conclusion, adds practitioner take-away prose and new subsections, updates the title and author information, changes citation style and removes the acknowledgments.

P2.justification: V2 adds deep-result, F1 and neural-configuration tables, a critical-difference diagram and paired radar plots. Scorer plots gain MixVal panels, and Figure 1 adds source overlays and an illustrated invariant subspace. The document also receives a dedicated title page, different typography and substantially reformatted tables and captions.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful deep comparisons, training details, F1 robustness evidence and scorer significance tests. However, new inconsistencies weaken their reliability: v1's main and appendix Mushroom tables agree on ClassRegOT accuracy of 0.82, whereas v2 reports 0.82 in Table 2 and 0.62 in Table 13 without explanation. Section 4.3 also says DANN improves all datasets despite Table 3 reporting BCI accuracy of 0.41 versus 0.54 for Train Src. These problems, together with single-split deep evaluation, prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
